references.text: Repeats that the children of Israel did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron, the same formula of obedience as in verse 28.
Moses and Aaron did as the Lord had commanded them, the same pattern of obedience to God's command.
The children of Israel did everything just as the Lord had commanded Moses, the same formula of obedience used regarding the construction of the tabernacle.
Moses did in all things just as the Lord had commanded him, showing the same pattern of faithful obedience.
The children of Israel celebrated Passover just as the Lord had commanded Moses, a direct link to the Passover command and obedience.
Concerns righteousness through keeping all the commands just as the Lord has commanded, the same principle of obedience.
By faith Moses kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, referring to Israel's obedient celebration of Passover.
Creates a theological parallel by showing that the pattern of obedience from the departure at Passover is repeated in the setting up of the tent.
Highlights the continuity of obedience from the Exodus to the entry into the land (Joshua), where the same principles apply.
Establishes a thematic parallel between obedience at the celebration of Passover and obedience at the building of the tabernacle.
Shows that the principle of collective obedience to God's specific command to the leaders also applies to the consecration of the Levites.
Expands the understanding of obedience from ritual action to daily life and travel arrangements during the wilderness journey.
Connects the principle of complete obedience to the establishment of the priesthood, parallel to the celebration of Passover.
